description: Phase-TJ — port TokenJuice (rule-based tool-output compaction) to Go for Aura. Plan in docs/tokenjuice-aura-integration-plan.md (~13 KB, 11 sections). Algorithm spec in docs/tokenjuice-algorithm-spec.md. Rules catalog in docs/tokenjuice-rules-catalog.md. Test strategy in docs/tokenjuice-test-strategy.md. License: openhuman Rust port is GPLv3 — DO NOT copy .rs source. Rewrite from algorithm spec in Go. Upstream vincentkoc/tokenjuice MIT but easier to write 10 starter rules from scratch. Insertion at internal/agent/executor.go:92-94 (NOT loop.go) — before WrapUntrustedToolResult + limitToolContent. Single new dep github.com/rivo/uniseg (MIT, pure Go). 8 stories, 6-9 days estimated. After Phase-TJ: heavy-turn tool outputs auto-compacted, raw-JSON-echo bug stabilized (model never sees the blob), context-pressure reduced, tool budget effectively extended. Discovered need 2026-05-18 evening live in Telegram chat 1148481707: Aura dumped raw JSON of file action=read TOOLS.md (7112 chars) as her reply. TJ would compact to <100 chars metadata + head excerpt before the model sees it.

userStories.title: Classify algorithm — rule matching with score-based selection
userStories.description: Implement classify.go per docs/tokenjuice-algorithm-spec.md §3 Algorithm — classify. Score-based: priority*1000 + argv0*100 + commandIncludes*10 + toolNames*5. Best-match wins. Pseudocode in Go: func ClassifyExecution(input Input, rules []*CompiledRule) ClassificationResult. Returns matched rule + score, or nil rule + score=0 if no match. Add 1 hardcoded fallback rule in builtin/fallback.json (passes through with head/tail clamp at 200/200 chars) to exercise end-to-end. Unit tests cover: empty rules → nil match; single rule single match → that rule; competing rules → highest score wins; toolNames filter; commandIncludes filter; stdoutMatches regex filter.

userStories.notes: Algorithm spec is the source of truth. The fallback rule unlocks E2E testing in US-TJ03 even before vendoring all 10 rules. Use Go's regexp/RE2 (NOT regexp/syntax with lookbehind) — all openhuman rules are RE2-compatible per spec.

userStories.title: Reduce pipeline + text helpers (graphemes, ANSI, dedupe, head/tail)
userStories.description: Implement reduce.go (main reduction) and text.go (helpers) per docs/tokenjuice-algorithm-spec.md §4 Reduce + §5 Text helpers. Pipeline order: strip_ansi → normalize_lines → dedupe_adjacent → head_tail/clamp. Grapheme-aware clamp via github.com/rivo/uniseg (the perf hotspot — use byte-index iteration, not materialised cluster slice, per spec). Pass-through safety: MIN_COMPACT_INPUT_BYTES=512, MIN_COMPACT_RATIO=0.95 (skip compaction if input < 512B or ratio > 0.95). Failure-preserving: if exit_code != 0, use rule.failure.head/tail if present. Unit tests: tiny input passthrough, oversized input compact, CJK preserved (no UTF-8 boundary cut), ANSI stripped, dedup adjacent identical lines, head+tail with '(N more)' middle elision.

userStories.notes: Grapheme clamp is THE hotspot per spec — uniseg.GraphemeBoundaries with byte iteration is faster than uniseg.Step + slice materialization. Bench BEFORE optimizing.

userStories.title: Measurement — baseline cmd/probe_chat suite with vs without TokenJuice

(e) Write findings to docs/tokenjuice-measurement-2026-05-18.md. Success criterion: ≥10% avg token reduction with 0 probe regressions.
